title: Luka Dončić sets Lakers career high with 60 points, continuing his recent dominance
content:
MIAMI — Luka Dončic scored 60 points — a personal high since he joined the Los Angeles Lakers midway through last season — to lead his team to its eighth straight win on the second night of a difficult back-to-back against the Miami Heat.

Dončić’s huge game, combined with LeBron James’ triple-double on the night he tied the record for most games played in NBA history, pushed the Lakers (45-25) past the Heat 134-126.

Dončić, who was questionable to play after the Lakers beat the Rockets in Houston on Wednesday night, brought the Lakers back from as many as 15 points down with an absurd array of shot-making.

After scoring 21 points in the first half, setting the Lakers’ single-season record for most 3s made in the process, Dončić caught fire in the second half. He made 11-of-16 from the field, including a dagger fading 3 in front of the Heat bench.

He made 9 of 17 from beyond the arc in the game.

Dončić attempted 19 free throws, 24 fewer than Miami’s Bam Adebayo did in his 83-point game earlier this month. The Lakers bench celebrated when Dončić drew a foul in the final seconds, giving him a chance to reach 60. They groaned when he missed the first free throw but erupted when he made the second.

The team, including James, mobbed Dončić after the game. Before leaving the court, he posed for pictures with tennis star Carlos Alcaraz.
